recent_articles.title: Scorching days, restless nights: Heatwave tightens grip across parts of India - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** experienced scorching temperatures exceeding 44° Celsius in several regions, prompting **hospitals** in Punjab to activate heat stroke management units. The **IMD** issued heatwave alerts for three districts of Jharkhand and warned of rising temperatures across Delhi, Haryana, and Chandigarh.  Veterinarians and animal rescuers reported an increase in distressed birds and animals suffering from dehydration and heatstroke. In Himachal Pradesh, a yellow warning for heatwave conditions was issued for parts of the state. **Chief Ministers** of various states ordered officials to ensure adequate drinking water availability, while **Congress leader Kishori Lal Sharma** raised concerns about power supply disruptions in Uttar Pradesh's Amethi constituency.

recent_articles.title: JMM, Cong. bid to divide society, undermine tribal rights won’t succeed: BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Babulal Marandi**, leader of the **BJP** in the Jharkhand Assembly, criticized the ruling **JMM** and **Congress** for engaging in divisive politics. He accused them of opposing the "Adivasi Samagam" and claiming that tribal communities are being converted to Hindus.  Marandi asserted that these claims are false and that there is no tradition of making someone a Hindu. He also alleged that the ruling party is trying to undermine tribal traditions and customary systems for vote-bank politics, and vowed to prevent their success.

recent_articles.title: 12 MPs, four Parliamentary panels selected for Sansad Ratna Awards - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Prime Point Foundation** has selected **12 MPs** and four Parliamentary Committees for this year's Sansad Ratna Awards.  **Jagdambika Pal**, **P.P. Chaudhary**, **Nishikant Dubey**, and **Shrikant Eknath Shinde** are among the individuals recognized, while the **Committee on Agriculture**, **Finance Committee**, **Rural Development and Panchayati Raj Committee**, and **Coal and Mines Committee** have also been awarded for their performance.

recent_articles.title: A.P. continues to grapple with intense heat as 95 mandals record above 42°C - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Andhra Pradesh** continues to experience intense heat, with 95 out of 688 mandals recording temperatures above 42°C.  The highest temperature reached 45.8°C at Kanumolu in Krishna district. While some districts received light to moderate rainfall on Saturday, severe heatwave conditions are expected for 21 mandals and widespread heatwave conditions for 214 mandals on Sunday. The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** predicts that weather systems brewing over the Bay of Bengal may bring isolated showers with lightning and thunderstorms in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema next week, but this activity is not expected to be widespread.

recent_articles.title: Sebi bars seven entities in social media stock recommendations, alleges Rs 58 crore gains - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sebi**, India's market regulator, has accused seven individuals and a group of entities, including Rohan Gupta and Sharon Gupta, of manipulating stock prices through social media influence. The regulator conducted searches between January 21-24, 2026, after observing unusual trading patterns linked to the group's online activity. **Sebi** alleges that the group accumulated shares before recommending them on social media platforms, profiting from price increases following retail investor participation in those stocks.  The regulator found a significant increase in trade value and profits for the group during the examination period.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Field visits for house-listing, household data collection begin in Jharkhand - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Jharkhand** began the first phase of its 2027 Census on May 16, 2026.  Trained enumerators will visit homes across the state's 24 districts and 32,459 villages to collect data on housing conditions, family details, and assets. The exercise, which runs until June 14, 2026, has deployed over 76,000 government officers and employees, including field trainers, enumerators, and supervisors.  **Jharkhand's Directorate of Census Operations** is overseeing the process.

recent_articles.title: UN event highlights India-Oman maritime ties through maiden voyage of stitched sail vessel - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Indian Navy**'s traditional stitched sail vessel, **INSV Kaundinya**, embarked on its maiden voyage from Porbandar to Muscat. The event, organized by the **Permanent Mission of India to the UN** and the **Oman Mission to the UN**, highlighted centuries-old maritime traditions and cooperation amidst global shipping disruptions.  Indian Navy Commodore Amit Srivastava, Commander Vikas Sheoran who skippered the vessel, and Expedition Officer Commander Y. Hemant Kumar attended the event. The voyage underscores India's ancient maritime trade routes connecting India with the Arabian Peninsula and East Africa, while Oman's Permanent Representative to the UN Omar Said Omar Alkathiri emphasized the shared history and the importance of cooperation in ocean governance.

recent_articles.title: Congress leader and former Jharkhand Minister, Alamgir Alam, walks out of jail - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Alamgir Alam**, a former Jharkhand minister, was released on bail from the Birsa Munda Central Jail in Ranchi after the Supreme Court granted relief in his money laundering case.  The **Enforcement Directorate (ED)** arrested **Alam** and his OSD, Sanjiv Kumar Lal, in 2024 following the seizure of nearly ₹32.20 crore from a flat linked to them. The Congress party fielded Alam's wife, Nishat Alam, as their candidate for the Pakur Assembly constituency in the 2024 elections, where she won. **Babulal Marandi**, the Leader of Opposition in the Jharkhand Assembly, criticized the celebration surrounding Alam's release, stating that it was premature and did not equate to an acquittal. He emphasized that the trial is ongoing and the legal process will continue until a final verdict is reached.

recent_articles.title: SC asks Centre to consider States’ pleas for funds for CCTVs in police stations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** urged the **Union government** to fully implement the Assistance to States and Union Territories for Modernisation of Police (ASUMP) scheme, which provides funds for installing CCTV cameras in police stations and a centralized monitoring dashboard. The court expressed concerns over non-functional CCTV cameras in Udaipur police stations and directed the Centre to consider requests from states for funding.  The ASUMP scheme has been extended until September 30, 2026, with most states initiating steps towards compliance. However, Jharkhand was criticized for not installing any CCTV cameras, despite receiving funds under the scheme. The court also cautioned against releasing funds without due diligence to prevent misappropriation.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Palnadu police bag top CEIR award for recovering lost mobile phones - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Department of Telecommunications (DoT)** presented CEIR Awards to police units in Palnadu, NTR, and Eluru districts for their successful mobile phone recovery efforts. **DoT Deputy Director General Hemant Rathwe**, along with **Director General of Police Harish Kumar Gupta**, awarded the top three positions to **Palnadu district Superintendent of Police B. Krishna Rao**, **NTR Police Commissioner S.V. Rajasekhar Babu**, and **Eluru district SP K. Pratap Shiva Kishore**.  The awards recognize the police units' contributions in recovering a significant number of lost mobile phones using the CEIR platform.

recent_articles.title: IPO Calendar: 2 issues to keep investors busy but mainboard activity remains muted - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **RFBL Flexi Pack**, a Gujarat-based company that manufactures and trades printed multilayer flexible packaging materials, is raising Rs 35.33 crore through an IPO of 70.65 lakh shares. The company plans to use the proceeds for capital expenditure, working capital needs, and general corporate purposes.  **Goldline Pharmaceutical**, another company seeking to raise Rs 11.61 crore through a fresh issue of 27 lakh shares, operates an asset-light pharmaceutical marketing business selling medicines under its "Goldline" brand across various segments. The company plans to use most of the IPO proceeds toward repayment of borrowings.

recent_articles.title: Three IT employees held with MDMA in Hayathnagar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Three IT employees**, Anjad, Hemant, and Harish, were arrested in Hayathnagar for possession and alleged sale of MDMA. The **Excise State Task Force** seized 7.44 grams of the drug during an operation that was led by CI Biksha Reddy and SSI Balaraju.  The accused allegedly procured MDMA from Bengaluru and sold it in Hyderabad at varying prices, with Hemant financing the operation. Further investigation is underway to identify other individuals involved in the supply network.

recent_articles.title: Police arrest Maoist leader from Jharkhand’s Latehar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ranchi Rural SP Gaurav Goswami** arrested a 42-year-old sub-zonal commander of the banned **Tritiya Sammelan Prastuti Committee (TSPC)** in Jharkhand's Latehar district. The man, with 16 pending criminal cases against him, was apprehended after police received a tip-off about his presence at his Chandwa residence. During the raid, authorities recovered weapons and other items from his possession.  The arrested individual provided names of his squad associates who are either in custody or deceased.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Around 82 lakh households have opted for self enumeration as field visits begin in 5 states - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union government** announced that over 82 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the initial Houselisting and Housing Operations (HLO) phase of Census 2027. The exercise, which commenced on May 1st in several states including Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan, aims to collect data about household facilities and demographics.  The HLO will continue until May 30th, with trained enumerators visiting each house for verification.

recent_articles.title: Hemant Soren launches self-enumeration phase of Census 2027 in Jharkhand - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hemant Soren**, **Chief Minister of Jharkhand**, launched the self-enumeration phase of Census 2027, urging residents to participate actively.  He emphasized that the census data will guide future welfare schemes and ensure efficient delivery of benefits.  The process will continue until May 15th, with house-listing and housing census operations from May 16th to June 14th. **Prabhat Kumar**, Director of the Directorate of Census Operations (Government of India), also participated in the self-enumeration.  **Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar** and **Aditya Sahu**, **BJP State president**, also recorded their details, highlighting the importance of census data for policymaking and development planning.

recent_articles.title: Woman found dead in decomposed state - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A 34-year-old woman, **Pooja Dutta**, was found dead in her Adugodi residence on Monday after neighbors reported a foul odor.  **Dutta**, who worked for a private company, was discovered naked and in a decomposed state, raising suspicion of foul play. The police are investigating the circumstances surrounding her death, which may have occurred two to three days prior, and are examining evidence including an old company ID card and torn papers found in the house.  The investigation will focus on identifying the man who visited **Dutta** frequently and analyzing her recent call records and social circle.

recent_articles.title: Coal India Q4 Results: Profit rises 12% to Rs 10,908 crore; co declares Rs 5.25 dividend - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Coal India** reported a 12% increase in profit before tax for the quarter, reaching Rs 14,627 crore. The company declared a final dividend of Rs 5.25 per share, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming AGM. Revenue rose 8% to Rs 51,618 crore, driven by higher realizations despite flat sales volumes.  Expenses increased due to higher levies and finance costs, leading to a 12% decline in profit after tax for FY26 to Rs 31,071 crore.

recent_articles.title: Court can reject anticipatory bail but cannot direct accused to surrender: Supreme Court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** ruled that a court cannot compel an accused to surrender before trial after rejecting their anticipatory bail. The court upheld the Jharkhand High Court's decision, which had rejected the accused's second anticipatory bail plea and directed him to surrender and seek regular bail.  The case involved allegations of cheating, forgery, and other offenses related to a land dispute.

recent_articles.title: Election Commission, and not the BJP, seems to be fighting Trinamool in West Bengal, says Kapil Sibal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kapil Sibal**, a senior Supreme Court lawyer and Rajya Sabha MP, criticized the **Election Commission of India (ECI)**'s actions in West Bengal ahead of the upcoming elections. He accused the **EC** and the **BJP** of working together to suppress the Trinamool Congress (TMC), alleging an "unconstitutional Emergency" and a disproportionate deployment of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF).  Other opposition leaders, including **Arvind Kejriwal**, have also expressed concern over the situation.

recent_articles.title: Govt claims women winning unreserved panchayat seats in ‘significant numbers’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Government** celebrated National Panchayati Raj Day, highlighting the progress of women's reservation in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).  While the Constitution mandates a 33% quota for women in urban and rural local bodies, 19 states have extended this provision to reserve 50% seats for women. However, data shows that the actual number of women representatives exceeds the prescribed quota in only 10 states/union territories, while four others fail to meet it.  The Ministry emphasized the increasing representation of women in PRIs, but acknowledged discrepancies between mandated and achieved quotas across various states.

recent_articles.title: Adani Power shares zoom nearly 40% in just 13 sessions. Should you book profits now? - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Adani Power**, India's largest private thermal power producer, is experiencing strong bullish momentum in its share price. The stock has recently broken out of a consolidation phase with expanding volumes and positive momentum across the **Adani Group**.  Traders are encouraged to hold existing long positions and view dips as buying opportunities. Analysts anticipate rising power demand due to the receding western disturbance that disrupted March's peak, which will benefit companies like **Adani Power** and NTPC.

recent_articles.title: PM Modi’s jhalmuri break in Jhargram leaves Trinamool fuming - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** enjoyed a break from public meetings in West Bengal by savoring jhalmuri, a Bengali snack. **Mr. Modi** shared photos and videos of the encounter with a local vendor who initially declined his offer to pay. The **Trinamool Congress**, which is facing criticism for its handling of tribal issues, stated that the Prime Minister's visit extended the schedule in Jhargram and prevented the arrival of Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren and his wife Kalpana Soren.

recent_articles.title: Chhattisgarh Vedanta power plant blast: Death toll rises to 24 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A blast at the Vedanta power plant in Chhattisgarh's Sakti district has tragically claimed 24 lives, with one more fatality reported on Sunday.  **Vedanta Ltd.** workers were injured when a steel tube carrying high-pressure steam exploded, leaving several others critically burned. **Anil Agarwal**, chairman of **Vedanta Group**, and **Devendra Patel**, plant head, are among eight to ten individuals named in an FIR filed by police for causing death by negligence.  The incident is under investigation by both the police and state authorities.

recent_articles.title: Chhattisgarh power plant explosion death toll touches 23 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Vedanta** group chairman **Anil Agrawal** and others have been booked under BNS sections 106(1), 289, and 3(5) in connection with the explosion at a power plant in Chhattisgarh's Sakti district that killed 23 people.  The incident occurred on April 14, 2026, after an excessive accumulation of fuel inside the boiler furnace caused extreme pressure to build up, leading to the explosion of the tube connecting the boiler to the turbine. **Naveen Jindal**, industrialist and Lok Sabha MP, has come out in support of **Agrawal**, arguing that he had no role in the plant's operations and that the "Viksit Bharat" vision needs investors like him to keep investing and building.

recent_articles.title: Heatwave alert in Maharashtra till April 20; Akola hottest at 44.2°C - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** has issued heatwave alerts for six states, including Maharashtra, where temperatures are expected to rise by 1-2°C over the next three days. The highest recorded temperature in the country so far is 44.2°C in Akola district.  **Dr. Pradeep Awate**, former State Surveillance Officer, Maharashtra Health Services, attributes the rising temperatures to concrete projects and a decline in trees, which are contributing to increased heat in Mumbai. **Bikram Singh**, chief scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre, stated that the IMD is vigilant and has already sent alerts regarding the heatwave conditions. The Maharashtra Government has implemented standard operating procedures (SOPs) to address the impact of the heatwaves, including regulating working hours during peak temperatures.

recent_articles.title: It’ a red-letter day, says Revanth; KTR blames BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the defeat of the Women's Reservation Bill in Parliament, **Congress** and **Bharatiya Rashtra Samithi (BRS)** leaders praised opposition parties for uniting to block the controversial legislation.  **Rahul Gandhi**, **Mallikarjun Kharge**, and **A. Revanth Reddy** led the charge against the bill, with **K. T. Rama Rao** blaming the BJP for its failure. **Bandi Sanjay** accused the Congress of using the bill to weaken southern India, while **N Ramchander Rao** criticized the bill's defeat as a setback for women's empowerment.

recent_articles.title: Four Maoists killed in exchange of fire with security forces in Jharkhand - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Jharkhand Police** and the **209 COBRA Battalion** conducted a joint operation in the forest region between Hazaribagh and Chatra, resulting in the deaths of four Maoists.  The deceased included **Shahdev Mahto**, a regional committee member with a ₹15 lakh reward; **Ranjit Ganjhu**, a zonal committee member with a ₹10 lakh reward; **Natasha**, a sub-zonal committee member with a 17-case record; and **Budhan Karmali**, an area commander with a ₹1 lakh reward.  The operation also recovered weapons and other items of daily use, according to the police who claim it has neutralized the Maoist squad active in the region. The police have appealed for remaining militants to surrender.
